newsitem.title: USA: Sotheby's to auction Windsor collection.
newsitem.headline: Sotheby's to auction Windsor collection.

text.p: Sotheby's auction house announced on Monday it was selling the contents of the Paris home of the Duke and Duchess of Windsor, the couple whose love shook the British monarchy 60 years ago.

The collection of more than 40,000 items reveals the personal and public life of King Edward VIII, who abdicated in 1936 to wed Wallis Warfield Simpson, an American who had previously been married twice.

The sale over 18 sessions from Sept. 11 to 18 in New York includes the George III mahogany library table, circa 1755, upon which the king signed away his inheritance, and the 78 rpm recording of his farewell address on BBC radio.

Sotheby's called the collection "perhaps the greatest treasure house of royal possessions offered at auction." It estimates the total sale of furniture, paintings, decorations, books, photographs, coins, medals and clothing at $5 million to more than $7 million, with the proceeds going to charities.

"This is a collection really like no other," Joe Friedman, Sotheby's head of English furniture who documented the possessions, said. "It has tremendous narrative power. Every object tells a story, each evokes a moment in the lives of the duke and duchess."
Love letters and a piece of the couple's wedding cake will be put on the block along with anniversary presents and tokens of love that passed between them throughout their marriage.
The collection was acquired after the death of the duchess in 1986 by Mohamed Al Fayed, chairman of Harrods of London and proprietor of L'Hotel Ritz in Paris. The duke died in 1972.

Sotheby's said proceeds of the sale would go to the Alfayed International Charitable Foundation, which contributes to research on childhood diseases, hospitals and homes for orphans. Al Fayed said in a statement that he was selling the collection to make more room for his young and growing family, who had been using only the top floor of the Paris house.
The collection traces back through more than two centuries of royal history including the monarchies of most of the countries of Europe and Japan, Friedman said.

Edward VIII became king in January 1936 after the death of his father, George V, but his reign was short. He decided to abdicate in December because of the general disapproval of his proposed marriage to divorcee Simpson.

"You must believe me when I tell you that I have found it impossible to carry the heavy burden of responsibility and discharge my duties as king as I would wish to do without the help and support of the woman I love," he declared in his farewell address.

The unprecedented constitutional crisis had played out in private before the abdication and the announcement shocked Britain and much of the world. Edward's brother, the Duke of York, became King George VI.

Edward was given the title of Duke of Windsor and married Simpson in June 1937. The couple played an active role in public life and were leaders of society and important figures in 20th century fashion.

Sotheby's clothing and couture expert Kerry Taylor told reporters the duke was arguably the most fashionable man of the century and described his wardrobe in the collection as "historically, the most important male wardrobe ever to come to auction."
